analysis: The method `readString` reads a line from a `BufferedReader` and then extracts a substring from it. The substring is obtained by calling `line.substring(line.indexOf(":") + 1)`. The `substring` method is called with the index `line.indexOf(":") + 1` as the `beginIndex` parameter. According to the `substring` method's documentation, it throws an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the length of the string. In the given code, the `beginIndex` is calculated as `line.indexOf(":") + 1`. If the `line` does not contain the character `:`, `indexOf(":")` will return `-1`, and `beginIndex` will be `0`. If `indexOf(":")` returns a non-negative value, `beginIndex` will be a positive value. Therefore, the `beginIndex` can never be negative. However, if `indexOf(":")` returns a value that, when incremented, is greater than the length of the string, an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` will be thrown. This condition is not checked in the code, and hence, the `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is not avoided.
remark: The `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is not avoided and can be thrown if the `line` contains the character `:`, but the position of `:` is at the last character of the string. In this case, `line.indexOf(":") + 1` will be equal to the length of the string, and `substring` will throw an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
